name: Maunakea Observatories
description: A group of independent observatories on the summit of Maunakea, at about 4,205 m, observing in optical, infrared and submillimeter wavelengths. Twelve facilities house thirteen telescopes with mirrors from 0.9 to 25 m, including the twin Keck telescopes, Subaru and the James Clerk Maxwell Telescope.
highlights: The University of Hawaii 2.24 m telescope had first light in 1970, starting the site's growth as an international observatory.
Keck I had first light on 24 November 1990 and Keck II on 27 April 1996; each has a mirror of 36 hexagonal segments.
Research here contributed to the 2011 Nobel Prize in Physics for the accelerating expansion of the universe.
